sections.label: Paralympians' medals and contingent size
sections.summary: Singapore's Paralympians won two Gold and one Bronze, with 13 athletes competing across six sports and 21 events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Adding to an already impressive haul of one Gold, two Silvers and three Bronzes from past Games, our Paralympians brought home another two Gold and one Bronze medals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This year, we had 13 athletes qualifying and representing Singapore across six sports and 21 events, almost double the contingent of eight athletes at the 2012 Paralympic Games.

sections.label: Yip Pin Xiu's two Golds
sections.summary: Yip Pin Xiu, a friend and team-mate, achieved the feat of clinching two Gold medals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Her good friend and team-mate, Yip Pin Xiu, achieved the extraordinary feat of clinching two Gold medals.

sections.label: Pin Xiu most decorated athlete
sections.summary: Pin Xiu now has three Paralympic Golds, making her the most decorated Team Singapore athlete at the Olympics and Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Pin Xiu now has three Paralympic Golds, making her the most decorated Team Singapore athlete at the Olympics and Paralympics.

sections.label: Team behind the Team support
sections.summary: The Singapore Sports Institute provides sports medicine, sports science and physiotherapy services so Paralympians can train and compete with peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our Paralympians' achievements would not be possible without the "Team behind the Team".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Special recognition and thanks must also go to the team at the Singapore Sports Institute, who work tirelessly to provide our athletes with the best system of support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This includes access to sports medicine, sports science and physiotherapy services, so that our Paralympians can train and compete with peace of mind and in the best possible conditions.

sections.label: Inspired by Theresa Goh's bronze
sections.summary: After watching his idol Theresa Goh clinch bronze, a son hopes to swim in the Paralympics one day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: After watching his idol Theresa Goh clinch the bronze medal, he is now filled with hope that, one day, he, too, can swim in the Paralympics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We hope that our son is inspired   and learns that nothing is impossible." Our Paralympians have certainly become our nation's sporting heroes, and I believe they will continue to inspire many more Singaporeans in time to come.

sections.label: Thirteen athletes at Rio Games
sections.summary: Thirteen athletes represented Singapore at the Rio Paralympic Games, showing a never-say-die attitude.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Not only did you compete and flew our flag with pride, you opened our eyes to show us what a "never-say-die" attitude is all about, both in the arena and outside of it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This year, 13 of you represented us at the recent Rio Paralympic Games.

sections.label: Paralympian's perseverance and achievements
sections.summary: She persevered to inspire other Singaporeans facing similar challenges, growing from a child unfamiliar with para-sports to a world record holder with three gold medals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: What made her persevere is the desire to inspire other Singaporeans facing similar challenges through her actions and achievements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: She has grown from a child who did not know much about para-sports to eventually becoming a world record holder with three gold medals to her name.

sections.label: Call for inclusive journey
sections.summary: The speaker says the audience played an instrumental part in becoming a better people and society, and calls on all Singaporeans to play an active role in this inclusive journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: You have all certainly played an instrumental part in our journey to become a better people and a better society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: I call on all Singaporeans to play an active role in this inclusive journey.

sections.label: Simple inclusive daily actions
sections.summary: It lists simple actions such as giving way on the MRT, helping others board the bus, and not parking in accessible lots meant for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Just simple actions, like giving way while on the MRT, providing assistance to board the bus, not parking in accessible lots meant for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Yip Pin Xiu on pushing limits
sections.summary: Double-gold medallist Yip Pin Xiu shared that doing one's best and pushing beyond one's limits is key and should be celebrated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In fact, double-gold medallist Yip Pin Xiu shared how doing one's best and pushing beyond their limits is key and should be celebrated.

sections.label: Theresa Goh describes Rio feelings
sections.summary: Theresa Goh, a bronze medallist also from the pool, described how she felt in Rio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Theresa Goh, bronze medallist, also from the pool, described how she felt in Rio.

sections.label: Rio 2016 Paralympics Team celebration
sections.summary: The Rio 2016 Paralympics Team won three medals, an Olympic record and two World records, and the largest ever contingent of 13 athletes competed in six sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From the Rio 2016 Paralympics Team, we have not one but two medallists, not two but three medals, an Olympic record and two World records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What we are also celebrating are the sporting values of participation; perseverance through adversity; and the personal integrity to better one self for a greater cause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To all the Paralympians, you and the sturdy will you possess are miracles personified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: We sent our largest ever contingent to the Paralympic Games with 13 athletes taking part in a record number of six sports, and our athletes were brilliant out there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our Paralympians gave us so many memories – from swimmers Theresa Goh winning the bronze medal to Yip Pin Xiu clinching two gold medals and smashing a world record in the process.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice unsung heroes campaign
sections.summary: NTUC FairPrice launched a campaign featuring four local personalities to reveal their unsung heroes who contributed to their personal development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Last year, NTUC FairPrice launched a campaign featuring four local personalities to reveal their unsung heroes who have contributed to their personal development.

sections.label: Congratulations to Paralympians and families
sections.summary: The speaker congratulates Paralympians, ambassadors, families and support staff, and notes one person's wish to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: You've shown me that all this hard work you've done is not only for yourself but for everyone around you.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And I want to do the same." And with this, my heartiest congratulations again to all our Paralympians, our ambassadors on the world stage and all the families and support staff behind the scenes.

sections.label: Norsilawati and Nur Syahidah training
sections.summary: Norsilawati trained six times a week while working as a freelance web designer and entered the Rio games at 39; Nur Syahidah trained six days a week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Take the feat of Norsilawati who trained six times a week while working as a freelance web designer; who entered the Rio games at the age of 39, undaunted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Or archery athlete Nur Syahidah, born with cerebral palsy, who similarly trained six days a week and spent most of her non-working days on practice.

sections.label: The Purple Parade inclusion event
sections.summary: About 10,000 Singaporean residents joined in the city district to support inclusion and celebrate abilities in The Purple Parade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Last weekend, despite the rain, we had about 10,000 Singaporean residents from all abilities, all walks of life, join us in the city district to support inclusion and celebrate abilities in a movement known as The Purple Parade – a ground-up movement that gained the support of many, including our country's top leaders.

sections.label: Theresa and Pin Xiu Europe travel
sections.summary: Theresa is a Spice Girls' Club fan, and she and Pin Xiu travelled to Europe on their own using public transport without special state help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Theresa told me she is a Spice Girls' Club fan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: She and Pin Xiu just travelled to Europe, London, Burmingham, on their own, public transport, without any special help from the state.

sections.label: Singapore Paralympic medals progress
sections.summary: At the 2008 Summer Paralympics six athletes won four medals, and Singapore now has nine Paralympic medals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Twenty years later, at the 2008 Summer Paralympics, we sent six athletes and they brought home four medals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Twenty-eight years on, from our first participation, we now have nine Paralympic medals.

sections.label: SDSC founding and 1974 selection
sections.summary: The SDSC was set up in 1973 by three ministries and eight disability organisations, and in 1974 selected two para-athletes for the Commonwealth Paraplegic Games.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The SDSC was set up in 1973 by the then Ministry of Social Affairs, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health and eight organisations for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1974, due to a shortage of funds, it selected only two para-athletes, Messrs Robert Tan and Frankie Thanapal, to represent Singapore at the Commonwealth Paraplegic Games in Dunedin, New Zealand.

sections.label: Prize money and equal treatment
sections.summary: The speaker argues prize money reflects how society values para-athletes' contributions and helps cover their costs, and that differing treatment reinforces barriers to an inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: You did not train and compete for that.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the prize money is important: whether we like it or not, it is a reflection of how society values the contributions that you have made and the lessons that you are sharing with us.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Aside from the reward, on a very practical basis, the prize money will help a para-athlete pay for transport, living expenses, the higher medical expenses, higher therapy fees, higher coaching fees, pay for your studies, pay for your other needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my letter to The Straits Times on 17 September 2008, I argued, and I reiterate now, that if we persist in having two different standards of treatment between athletes and para-athletes, we reinforce the erroneous perception that people with disabilities are not able and strengthen the barriers against building an inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot build a gracious inclusive society if we continue to deny the achievements of those perceived to be different and less able than we.

sections.label: Team Singapore international successes
sections.summary: Singaporeans have much to celebrate this year in Team Singapore's successes at the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, there is much for Singaporeans to celebrate this year in international sporting competitions, with Team Singapore's successes at the most prestigious international competitions – the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

sections.label: Yip Pin Xiu on para-sports effort
sections.summary: Ms Yip Pin Xiu said para-athletes put in the same effort and it is not easier being in para-sports, and para-athletes turn adversity into strength.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From the para-athletes' perspective, Ms Yip Pin Xiu was most generous when she said, "We put in the same amount of effort to get to where we are and it is not easier being in Para-sports." Despite what life has dealt them, para-athletes are experts at turning adversity into strength.

sections.label: Inclusive society and big dreams
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore would be poor if citizens with disabilities could not dream big or realise their potential, and must press on to leave no one behind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a country with one of the highest in terms of gross domestic product per capita in the world, we would be poor if our citizens with disabilities were not able to have big dreams or realise their full potential.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We thank those who have loved and supported them through their unique journeys.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must continue to press on to make Singapore a home where no one is left behind.
